title: ICT and income inequality: a cross-national perspective
decision_rationale: Panel of 109 countries, 2001-2014, own FE estimation of internet, broadband and mobile on Gini indices (family 4), with income-group splits.
exposure_measure: ITU internet users per 100, fixed broadband subscriptions per 100, mobile subscriptions per 100; lagged one year

sample.economies_or_groups: 109 countries, all development levels and regions
sample.income_groups_covered: high, upper-middle, lower-middle, low (low and lower-middle pooled)

design.estimator: Two-way fixed effects with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: Country and year FE; ln GDP pc and square, female LFP, urbanisation, birth rate, population 65+, governance indicators, secondary enrolment, health expenditure share; regressors lagged 1 year

heterogeneity.finding: Broadband raises Gini in middle- and high-income subsamples, barely detectable in low income; Mobile reduces Gini mainly in middle-income; InternetUse mostly insignificant in splits
Marginal effect of Broadband on Gini turns from negative at 25th percentile GDP pc to positive at 75th
ICT effects conditional on urbanisation, stability, governance, rule of law

income_group_results.lower_middle: pooled with low: Broadband n.s.; Mobile -0.014*/-0.011*; Internet n.s. (GiniNet), -0.091* (GiniMarket)

n_specifications_reported: about 10 (baseline, 3 interaction sets x 2 DVs, 3 splits x 2 DVs)

confounding_reverse_causation.why: One-year lags only; no instrument, causal-sounding language; inequality could drive adoption
confounding_reverse_causation.evidence: Section 3, p.198: 'lagged one year to guard against simultaneity bias'

exposure_measurement.why: Subscription/use per 100 are standard but crude proxies; mobile subs exceed 100 per 100

selection_of_countries_years.why: Unbalanced panel, 830 obs from 109 countries over 14 years because of SWIID coverage; short span

outcome_measurement.why: SWIID imputed Gini, mean of 100 imputations; imputation error ignored

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: Quadratic GDP, many interactions chosen post hoc; collinearity noted; split-sample drops quadratic

selective_reporting.why: Only interactions with substantive implications reported; other controls tried and dropped

notes: Text says 107 countries in the introduction, 109 elsewhere. Table 2 Hausman p-value 0.011 for GiniMarket. Coefficients on Gini points per 1 unit of ICT per 100. No injected instructions found.
